signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Intervention
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.26, having broken sharply below its SMA20 (162.53) and SMA50 (161.34) following suspected Japanese intervention and a hawkish BoJ hold at 1.0%. The G10 scorecard confirms a dominant bilateral theme with JPY outperforming peers by +1.906% while the USD laggard average sits at -1.322%, creating a massive 3.228% spread. Despite a +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage supporting the USD, the options market is pricing aggressive downside protection with a strong 25d risk reversal of -2.53. COT data shows specs remain heavily net short JPY (lev_net -114,030), suggesting the current move is being fueled by a disorderly short-covering unwind. The pair now tests the SMA200 at 157.93 as the next major structural floor. Risk: Fed adopts a surprisingly hawkish tone in upcoming communications, reigniting the carry trade bid and stalling the JPY recovery.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD is trading at 0.5878, maintaining a bullish position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5786–0.5826) after a +1.80% weekly gain. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. This speculative positioning is further challenged by a strong positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +30.6, indicating that New Zealand macro data is consistently beating expectations. The combination of restrictive data and a hawkish central bank stance creates an asymmetric short-squeeze risk toward 0.6000 if specs begin to capitulate. The negative real rate of -1.56% remains a headwind for long-term holders but does not offset the immediate technical and data-driven momentum. Risk: RBNZ signals a pause at the September 2nd meeting, validating the existing speculative short thesis.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Data Surprise + Technical Resistance
signals.text: USD/CAD is holding at 1.4028, reversing recent declines as it tests the SMA50 resistance at 1.4046. While the Fed-BoC carry differential of +150bp structurally favors the USD, recent Canadian GDP data has outpaced forecasts, prompting analysts to lower BoC rate cut expectations. This shift is reflected in the positive Canadian ESI (+5.6) and a restrictive real rate of +0.17%. COT positioning shows a crowded spec short in CAD (lev_net -99,823), leaving the pair vulnerable to further downside if USD strength continues to fade across the G10 complex. A sustained break below the SMA50 and 1.4000 psychological level would signal a shift in the medium-term regime. Risk: US 10Y yields, currently at 4.735%, continue to climb, providing enough USD support to overcome the improving Canadian macro outlook.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Volatility + Retail
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7025, supported by its SMA20 (0.6974) and a 70bp carry advantage over the USD via the RBA's 4.35% policy rate. The options market is pricing in significant tail risk with an elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of +6.1%, as IV (12.5%) significantly exceeds HV30 (6.4%). Retail sentiment shows a strong 76% short bias, diverging from the COT leveraged fund net long position of +20,521. This institutional vs. retail divergence typically favors further upside, as retail traders continue to unsuccessfully fade the established bullish trend. The RBA's hiking bias and positive real rate of +0.39% provide a fundamental floor for the pair. Risk: A sharp contraction in WTI oil or broader commodity prices undercuts the AUD's terms-of-trade advantage.
